text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Constitutional court chairman Yekta Gungor Ozden says the court may reach a verdict within six months on a case aimed at closing down the ruling Islamist Welfare Party.
- State Minister Ufuk Soylemez says his past role in the country's privatisation process had brought him into conflict with the current Labour Minister Necati Celik.
MILLIYET

- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan denies he would hand office to his coalition partner Tansu Ciller in June after reports that she had reached an agreement on taking over the prime minister's post then.
- Leading trade unions and businessmen's organisations make a joint statement calling on the current Islamist-led government to resign.
HURRIYET
- President Suleyman Demirel says it is impossible for Ciller to take office ahead of schedule in 1998 without Erbakan withdrawing from office.
- The Turkish foreign ministry will not hand fugitive Cypriot tycoon Asil Nadir over to British justice.
YENI YUZYIL
- A gold mine under development near the western coastal town of Bergama reopens after being shut temporarily because of security concerns prompted by local protests.
- Tepe-Akfen-Flughagen Wien AG wins a tender to build a new international terminal, multi-storey car park and other buildings for Istanbul airport.
RADIKAL
- President Demirel approves a draft law that will enable married Turkish women to retain their maiden name.
CUMHURIYET
- The Turkish armed forces take control of the Atrush region in northern Iraq on the eighth day of a cross-border operation.
DUNYA
- Consumers will have to pay the price of government plans to grant large price subsidies to farmers.
- State-owned tobacco producer Tekel introduces a new cigarette to the market.
ZAMAN

- Soccer league champions Galatasaray turn down beer maker Tuborg's offer to produce a beer with their team colours printed on the can. Galatasaray's Istanbul rivals Fenerbahce and Besiktas agreed to take part in the project.
